reason: The Strassen proposals have the clearest potential to reduce arithmetic, but all seven 256-square helper calls pay their SME setup and exit costs, and timed packing, recombination, and FP32 error make the net result uncertain. The three workspace proposals largely describe the same candidate, so test that implementation once rather than treating aliases as independent evidence. Next rank the lower-risk tile mapping and FMOPA schedule changes; prior FMOPA-order results did not promote, and do not predict this different order. Panel packing has an unverified cache hypothesis; previous panel layouts did not promote. Transpose fusion may remove scratch traffic but adds repeated register transposes. Tail alignment and the C fallback affect general sizes, not the fixed n=512 timing path. The proposed paired-load post-index change has unverified instruction legality, so confirm the encoding before implementation or abstain. No recommendation here is a measured speedup.
